title: Specify the client's close response to server?
body:
### What is the issue with the WebSockets Standard?

(This issue is written by @domenic alone, but is based on only a tentative understanding of the underlying protocol, aided by GPT-6 Astra Extra High.)

When the server sends a shutdown message to a WebSocket, all browser clients apparently repeat the close reason text back to the server:

```
Server sends:       Close(code=1000, reason="server finished")
All browsers reply: Close(code=1000, reason="server finished")
```

This is apparently not required by the RFC; [section 5.5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455.html#section-5.5.1) says

```

   If an endpoint receives a Close frame and did not previously send a
   Close frame, the endpoint MUST send a Close frame in response.  (When
   sending a Close frame in response, the endpoint typically echos the
   status code it received.)
```

which is not very strong on normative requirements; it seems to say that echoing the code is "typical" (not "must"), and says nothing about the reason.

However, a recent change in WPT infrastructure requires this browser behavior: [`opening-handshake/005.html`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/c93bdbe1676032a83981d207390b4f6ceeb88a03/websockets/opening-handshake/005.html)'s [server handler](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/c93bdbe1676032a83981d207390b4f6ceeb88a03/websockets/handlers/simple_handshake_wsh.py#L17-L31) reads `len(close_frame) + MASK_LENGTH` bytes from the client, i.e., the number of bytes that would be sent by a client that echoes both code and reason.

https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/commit/d6d83998cdc31f3314f79d3d653f6d78be8a0b25 switched `pywebsocket3`'s base class from `CGIHTTPRequestHandler` to `SimpleHTTPRequestHandler` for Python 3.15 compatibility, which seems to have changed the behavior from allowing <= the number of read bytes before shutdown, to instead waiting until that many bytes is always read.

This means that clients which do not send back the exact same close message length as a browser, e.g., [Undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/) / Node.js (which sends back `Close(code=1000, reason="")`), will fail the WPT.

We should probably either:

1. Specify browser behavior in this case, in whatwg/websockets, as an extension of the RFC.
2. Loosen the test somehow. (It seems pretty delicate, given the comments in the server handler, but I'm sure some coding agent can figure it out.)

I lean toward (1). However, ChatGPT notes that interop is not as clear in cases like "empty close frames and cases where the client has already initiated closing".
